sections.title: Habit and identification
sections.text: Rudbeckia hirta, black-eyed Susan, is a North American annual, biennial or short-lived perennial. Its upright, hairy stems usually reach about 30–90 cm; the alternate leaves are rough and hairy.

sections.title: Flower heads and fruit
sections.text: Each flower head, about 5–8 cm across, has yellow ray florets around a raised dark-brown central disk. The dry fruits are small achenes. The plate correctly shows the hairy stems, characteristic flower heads and a fruiting head.

sections.title: Uses and caution
sections.text: It is grown mainly as an ornamental and for pollinators. The references consulted do not confirm food use; do not treat the flowers, leaves or seeds as food.
